description: Improvement backlog worked one item per iteration. Items too large for a single iteration are recorded here as stories with the notes needed to resume them. The SEO/GEO backlog in docs/SEO-GEO-STRATEGY.md is the companion document; this file tracks platform and engineering work.

stories.title: Remove duplicate SEO meta tags from the shell
stories.problem: index.html carried description, keywords, robots, canonical, Open Graph and Twitter tags, and SEO.jsx emits all of them through react-helmet. Helmet cannot remove tags it did not create, so every page shipped two of each. All 91 pages declared both their own URL and the site root as canonical; Google disregards conflicting rel=canonical entirely, and a crawler taking the first would fold the site onto the home page.
stories.resolution: All page-level tags removed from the shell; SEO.jsx owns them. <title> stays as the pre-JS fallback since Helmet replaces the single title element cleanly.
stories.verified: Three sample routes each carry exactly one description, canonical and og:title, with the canonical matching the page's own URL. Full audit: canonical mismatches fell from 86/87 to 12/87, and the 12 remaining are the pages tracked in SEO-2.

stories.title: Load Inter once, without blocking the first paint
stories.problem: Inter was requested twice from two different URLs: a <link rel=stylesheet> in index.html (weights 400-700) and an @import at the top of src/index.css (weights 300-700, and nothing on the site uses 300). The @import is the worse of the two - the browser cannot discover it until the CSS bundle has downloaded and parsed, so it serialises an extra round trip. The index.html link was render-blocking, and in a headless Chromium that could not reach Google Fonts the window load event never fired at all.
stories.resolution: Removed the @import. index.html now uses rel=preload as=style with an onload promotion to stylesheet, plus a noscript fallback. With display=swap the text was going to reflow regardless, so blocking first paint bought nothing.
stories.verified: Built CSS contains zero fonts.googleapis.com references (was 1). In headless Chromium the load event now fires; before this change page.goto with waitUntil load timed out at 30s on every route.

stories.title: Infinite render loop in AnalyticsProvider blanked every page
stories.problem: In a stock headless Chromium, every route on the site shows PageLoadingFallback forever. No h1 renders, document.title stays at the static index.html title, and <main> contains only the skeleton. The React.lazy promise resolves but the Suspense boundary never commits. Reproduces on the production build and the dev server alike.
evidence: Bisected by adding shell layers one at a time to a two-line dependency-free lazy component: bare React lazy rendered, +ErrorBoundary rendered, +Router rendered, +AnalyticsProvider hung.
stories.root_cause: addInteraction was memoised with `score` in its dependency array, while the page-view effect both called addInteraction and listed it as a dependency. Scoring a page view changed the score, which gave addInteraction a new identity, which re-ran the effect, which scored the page view again. The loop never settled.
stories.impact: Three separate failures from one cycle. The lead score passed 45,000 within a second of page load and climbed about 3,500 a second, writing localStorage every pass. A GA4 lead_scoring event fired on every pass, so the analytics this code exists to collect were being flooded with garbage. And the render loop starved React badly enough that lazy routes never finished suspending, so every page on the site showed the loading skeleton and nothing else - no heading, no content, and the static shell title instead of the page's own.
stories.resolution: Hold the running score in a ref so addInteraction can read it without depending on it. addInteraction now depends only on location.pathname.
stories.verified: Before: score 45,709 at t=1s, 59,878 at t=6s, main containing only PageLoadingFallback. After, on both the dev server and the production build: score stable at 2 (the dev figure - StrictMode double-invokes the effect), real h1, the page's own title, aria-busy gone, stable through t=8s.

stories.title: Repair PWA install and offline support
stories.problem: public/sw.js precached /favicon.ico and /IPS-blue.webp, neither of which ships. cache.addAll() is atomic, so install() rejected on every visit and the service worker never activated - the site had no offline support at all. manifest.json separately declared one 256x256 PNG as both 192x192 and 512x512, which fails Chrome's installability check, and marked it 'any maskable' with no safe-zone padding.
stories.resolution: Generated real 192/512 icons plus a padded maskable 512 and a 180 apple-touch icon into public/icons/. Rewrote manifest icons with matching sizes and split any/maskable purposes. sw.js now precaches individually via Promise.allSettled so one bad path degrades one asset instead of the whole worker, cache bumped to v2, navigation fallback serves the cached shell before the offline page. Registration gated to import.meta.env.PROD so the dev server stops serving stale bundles.
stories.verified: npm run build succeeds; every path in STATIC_ASSETS resolves to a file in dist/.

stories.title: Baseline security response headers
stories.problem: public/_headers carried only X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy. No HSTS, no Permissions-Policy, no CSP of any kind. Separately, hashed assets were cached for a year without 'immutable' so browsers still revalidated on reload, and unhashed files served from the site root (/icons/*, /IPSLogo.png) had no Cache-Control at all.
stories.resolution: Added Strict-Transport-Security (one year, apex only - includeSubDomains and preload are the domain owner's call once every subdomain is known HTTPS-only), Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'none', a deny-everything Permissions-Policy, and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin. Hashed /assets/* now immutable; unhashed statics get a revalidatable week; crawler files and the SPA shell stay short-lived.
stories.verified: _headers is syntactically a Cloudflare Pages rules file; every path pattern corresponds to a real file or directory in dist/.
stories.open: Add includeSubDomains, then preload, once the subdomain inventory is confirmed HTTPS-only.

stories.title: Pre-render routes to static HTML
stories.problem: The site is a client-rendered SPA - dist/index.html ships an empty <div id="root">. Google renders JS on a delay and a budget; several AI answer crawlers do not execute JS at all and see nothing. This is item 1 on the SEO/GEO backlog and the single largest remaining technical win.
notes: 94 routes in src/App.jsx, all React.lazy. scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs already parses that route table - reuse its extraction rather than writing a second parser.

react-helmet (not helmet-async) is in use. It has no server-side collection story that works cleanly with concurrent React 18; a headless-browser snapshot avoids the problem entirely because Helmet has already written the real <head>.

Cloudflare Pages runs the build, so the prerender step has to work in that container. Playwright/Puppeteer downloading Chromium at build time is the risk to settle first: measure install time and size, and have a fallback of prerendering only high-value routes.
This environment has Chromium at /opt/pw-browsers with PLAYWRIGHT_SKIP_BROWSER_DOWNLOAD=1, so local prototyping is free - do not mistake that for it working on Pages.

Split the work: (1) prototype a postbuild snapshot script locally and confirm rendered HTML contains real headings, meta and schema; (2) settle the Cloudflare build story; (3) wire it into the build and verify hydration does not warn.

stories.title: Clear the ESLint backlog
stories.problem: Roughly 795 pre-existing ESLint errors, dominated by missing react/prop-types and unused React imports. The noise means npm run lint is not usable as a gate, so new errors land unnoticed.
notes: Confirm the current count before starting; it predates several merges.
Unused React imports are mechanical under the automatic JSX runtime and can go in one pass.

react/prop-types on 39 components plus 98 pages is the bulk. Decide whether to fix or disable the rule - a site this size with no TypeScript may not earn prop-types - and record the decision rather than half-applying it.
Finish by making lint clean so it can be added to the build.

stories.title: Ship a real Content-Security-Policy
stories.problem: SEC-1 added only frame-ancestors, which cannot break rendering. A policy covering script-src, style-src, img-src and connect-src is the actual protection, and it is the one header on this site that will break pages if it is wrong.
notes: index.html has an inline gtag bootstrap, so script-src needs a nonce or a hash. Cloudflare Pages serves static files and cannot inject a per-request nonce - a build-time hash of the inline block is the workable route.

Origins to allow, taken from an audit of index.html and src/: googletagmanager.com and google-analytics.com (script, connect), fonts.googleapis.com (style) and fonts.gstatic.com (font), images.unsplash.com (img), calendly.com (frame, if the widget is embedded rather than linked).
framer-motion writes inline styles, so style-src almost certainly needs 'unsafe-inline'. Confirm before assuming it can be tightened.
Ship it as Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only first and watch for violations before enforcing. Do not enforce and verify in the same iteration.
Verify by loading the built site under a headless browser and asserting zero CSP violations in the console, not by reading the policy.

stories.title: Stop hotlinking hero images from Unsplash
stories.problem: 45 references to images.unsplash.com across src/. Page-critical imagery is served by a third party the site does not control: it is an extra DNS and TLS handshake in the LCP path, the URLs can change or 404, and it hands a third party a request log of every visitor.
notes: Inventory first: grep images.unsplash.com in src/ and record which are decorative and which are LCP candidates.
Check each image's Unsplash licence attribution requirement before self-hosting it.
Self-host as WebP/AVIF at the sizes actually rendered, with width/height set so layout does not shift.
Doing this properly is also the moment to add loading="lazy" and fetchpriority="high" on the one above-the-fold image per page.

stories.title: Stop tracking dist/ in git
stories.problem: dist/ is committed. Every build rewrites ~80 content-hashed chunk filenames, so an unrelated one-line source change produces a 160-file diff of deletions and additions that buries the real change in review.
notes: Cloudflare Pages builds from source, so the committed output is not what gets deployed - confirm that in CLOUDFLARE-DEPLOYMENT.md before removing it.
git rm -r --cached dist, add to .gitignore. History keeps the old blobs; that is fine and not worth a rewrite.

stories.title: Twelve resource guides render no SEO tags at all
stories.problem: 12 of the 18 pages under /resources import no SEO component. They have no title, no meta description and no canonical, so they all share the shell title and go to search engines with nothing describing them. These are keyword-targeted guides - it is the one page type where this matters most.
notes: No keywords prop was passed. SEO.jsx falls back to the site defaults, and meta keywords are slated for removal anyway (backlog item 9 in docs/SEO-GEO-STRATEGY.md).
stories.resolution: Added an SEO component to each of the 12, with a title, a description written from that page's own content, a canonical, and schemaType TechArticle. Titles are sized against the 23-character ' | Iowa Print Solutions' suffix that getPageTitle appends, so all 12 land at 44-56 characters rendered. Descriptions are 144-156 characters and all distinct. The PrinterLogic pages name Vasion Print first with the old name after, per the naming rule in CLAUDE.md; the URLs are unchanged.
stories.verified: All 12 routes on the production build: exactly one canonical and one description each, canonical matches the route, title under 60 characters, description 100-160 characters, 12 unique descriptions out of 12.

stories.title: Four pages crashed into the ErrorBoundary
stories.problem: /blog/papercut-hive-q4-2025-iowa, /industries/iowa-education-print-solutions, /industries/iowa-healthcare-print-solutions and /services/printerlogic-iowa time out waiting 20s for an h1 or h2 in <main>. Every other route renders in under a second. This is separate from SUSPENSE-1, which is fixed - these four still fail.
stories.root_cause: Three distinct bugs, all of the same class. PrinterLogicIowa used the lucide icon Cloud and PaperCutHiveQ42025Iowa used DollarSign without importing either. Both industry pages passed a JSX element to ServiceCard's icon prop, which destructures `icon: Icon` and renders <Icon />, so it needs a component reference. The healthcare page additionally used SmartLeadCTA without importing it, passing defaultCTA/urgentCTA/premiumCTA props that the component does not implement - it takes children, variant and size.
stories.resolution: Added the two missing icon imports. Changed the four ServiceCard icon props to component references, leaving the separate icon arrays as elements since those are consumed directly as {service.icon}. Rewrote the healthcare CTA section to use SmartLeadCTA as it is actually built, with real links and the real phone number from siteConfig.
stories.verified: All four routes now render a real h1 and 7-8 h2 sections with no pageerror, on the production build.
stories.follow_up: react/jsx-no-undef is already an error in eslint.config.js - it would have caught two of these. It was invisible among the ~795 existing errors. See LINT-1.

stories.title: 89 of 134 images have no width or height
stories.problem: Two thirds of the images on the site declare no intrinsic size, so the browser cannot reserve space before they load and the layout shifts. Cumulative Layout Shift is a Core Web Vital.
notes: Overlaps IMG-1 - the hotlinked Unsplash images are among the worst offenders and self-hosting them is the moment to set dimensions.
Prefer width/height attributes over CSS aspect-ratio so the reservation works before CSS parses.

stories.title: Titles and descriptions overflow their SERP limits
stories.problem: 86 of 87 page titles exceed 60 characters and 65 descriptions exceed 160, so Google truncates them mid-phrase. The call to action ends up cut off.
notes: SEO.jsx appends a site-name suffix to every title - measure the final rendered length, not the string passed in.
This is worth doing after SEO-2 so the 12 new pages are written to the limit rather than fixed twice.
The 12 resource guides from SEO-2 are already within limits and can be skipped.

stories.title: Heading levels skipped on 21 routes
stories.problem: 21 routes jump straight from h1 to h3. Screen reader users navigate by heading level, and a skipped level reads as a missing section.
notes: Not one shared component, which was the initial guess - the jumps came from three unrelated patterns.
The h4s nested under a real h3 in the same files were deliberately left alone; a blanket h4-to-h3 pass would have broken them.
stories.resolution:
Two layers. The visible one was a lead-in callout - 'Why this matters', 'Key Takeaways', 'Executive Summary' - marked h3 directly under the h1 on 19 pages; those became h2. Fixing them exposed a second layer the scanner had been hiding, because it only reports the first jump per page: 12 blog posts put an h4 checklist directly under an h2 section, skipping h3. Those became h3. Two h2->h4 cases were the same shape. One case was not a level problem at all. The hero card on the home page labelled a decorative product panel with an h3. Promoting it to h2 would have claimed a page section that does not exist, so it is a

with the same type scale.
stories.verified: Browser scan of all 91 routes: 0 heading jumps, down from 21. Every change rewrites the tag only; class names are untouched, so nothing moves visually.

stories.title: SmartLeadCTA discarded its callers' copy; templates imported from paths that did not exist
stories.problem: SmartLeadCTA accepts children, className, variant and size. EnhancedIndustryTemplate and EnhancedLocationTemplate call it with defaultCTA, urgentCTA and premiumCTA objects, which are silently discarded - the component renders the string 'Learn More'. The same call shape was on the healthcare page and is now fixed there.
stories.resolution: Implemented the defaultCTA/urgentCTA/premiumCTA API in SmartLeadCTA rather than stripping it from the callers - three call sites agreed on that shape, so the callers were right about what the component is for. Which tier renders is chosen from the visitor's lead grade via the real useLeadScoring in AnalyticsProvider; missing tiers fall back to defaultCTA. The children call shape still works. Removed the duplicate stub useLeadScoring that shadowed the real hook by name. Fixed every relative import in both page templates and replaced the invented (515) 123-4567 with siteConfig.business.phoneDisplay and phone.
stories.verified: /blog rendered a blue box reading 'Learn More' where its CTA copy should have been; it now renders the real CTA with the correct phone number. No occurrence of 123-4567 remains in src/. Every relative import in both templates resolves to a file on disk.

stories.title: Lead pipeline: one Pages Function that receives, stores and routes every lead
stories.problem: Iowa Print Solutions exists to produce leads for Infomax Office Systems, yet two of its three capture forms throw the lead away: PrintCostCalculator.jsx:111 and ResourceLibrary.jsx:122 show an alert() promising follow-up that never happens. Only Contact.jsx:56 posts anywhere (Formspree). The four calculators in Tools.jsx capture nothing. The rest of the site routes intent to 48 hard-coded mailto:DPearson@InfomaxOffice.com links, about 112 tel: links in three formats, and 10 bare calendly.com/pearsondan/30min links, none of which is recorded. Four 2025 posts (AIPrintManagementIowa2025, CloudPrintingSolutionsIowa2025, MobilePrintingSolutionsIowa2025, PrintManagementSoftwareROIIowa) still carry a placeholder phone number, tel:515-555-0123, and an unconfirmed info@iowaprintsolutions.com address. The outcome is one lead endpoint that every capture surface uses, a durable lead record, and an instant notification to Infomax sales carrying source page, tool inputs and the ips_lead_score AnalyticsProvider.jsx already computes. Every later LEAP story ends in this pipeline.
notes: AC1: functions/api/lead.js exists as a Cloudflare Pages Function. public/_routes.json already includes /* and excludes only static extensions, so /api/lead reaches the function without a routing change; confirm that in the built dist/_routes.json. It accepts POST JSON {type, name, email, company, phone, source, payload, leadScore, pagesViewed, consent}, validates server-side, and returns 400 with the failing field names.

AC2: Each accepted lead is written to a Cloudflare D1 table leads(id, created_at, type, source, contact fields, payload_json, lead_score, consent_basis, utm_json). The binding is declared in wrangler.toml (which today holds only name, compatibility_date and pages_build_output_dir). A write failure returns 5xx and the UI shows an error; it never shows success.

AC3: PrintCostCalculator.jsx submitLeadForm, ResourceLibrary.jsx handleDownload and Contact.jsx all submit through one src/utils/submitLead.js helper. No alert() remains in src/pages on a lead path (grep -n "alert(" src/pages returns none).
AC4: The payload includes ips_lead_score and ips_interactions read from localStorage inside try/catch, so sales sees the score that today never leaves the browser.
AC5: Infomax receives a notification per lead (transactional email or webhook) whose subject names lead type and source page. The credential is a Pages secret, never in the repo.
AC6: Turnstile token verified in the function plus a honeypot field; a submission without a valid token is rejected with 403 and no row.

AC7: The four placeholder tel:515-555-0123 links are replaced with siteConfig.business.phone, and info@iowaprintsolutions.com is replaced with the confirmed address unless Infomax confirms that mailbox exists (grep for 515-555-0123 in src/pages returns none).

AC8: A shared src/components/IntakeCTA.jsx replaces SmartCTA's mailto primaryAction in PerformanceComponents.jsx, Navbar.jsx gains a 'Free assessment' entry on desktop and mobile, and tel: links go through one helper that records a type='call_click' event with the page.

AC9: package.json gains a test script using node --test (no new dependency). tests/lead.test.mjs calls the function's onRequestPost with a stub D1 and asserts: a valid lead writes one row, a missing email returns 400 naming email, a failed write returns 5xx.

Competitive rationale: the Iowa dealers checked (Marco, Access Systems, Gordon Flesch, EO Johnson) end at a contact form or 'schedule a consultation'; a lead that arrives with tool inputs and an engagement score lets Infomax answer first and better scoped. https://www.marconet.com/ https://www.gflesch.com/cedar-falls-ia-copiers

Success metric: 0 alert-only or unrecorded lead paths; weekly leads by type and source measurable for the first time; target 3x the current Formspree-only weekly count within 60 days, measured against a baseline taken from Formspree before launch.

stories.title: Instant self-serve quote builder at /quote
stories.problem: No Iowa dealer checked publishes a price or an instant estimate; each ends in 'schedule a consultation'. National aggregators such as 1-800 Office Solutions publish lease and click-rate bands and capture cost-intent searches instead. Iowa Print Solutions has calculator parts, but they rest on unsourced constants: PrintCostCalculator.jsx:75-76 uses employees*15 implementation and employees*4*12 licensing in a misspelled licenseCoser, lines 56 and 65 hard-code a 0.25 efficiency gain, and Tools.jsx:41 applies a flat 25% savings that line 443 presents to visitors as an average. That breaks the repo's standing rule that every number carries a source. The outcome is a /quote flow (seats, device count and makes, mono and color monthly volume, product interest, on-prem or cloud, current lease payment) that returns a ballpark range built from Infomax-confirmed bands, with the national benchmark cited, and books an assessment in the same step.
notes: AC1: src/pages/Quote.jsx is routed at /quote in src/App.jsx and appears in the sitemap produced by scripts/generate-sitemap.mjs (which reads the App.jsx route table).

AC2: All price inputs come from a new src/config/pricing.js; each entry carries {low, high, unit, source, confirmedBy, asOf}. A pure function priceRange(inputs, pricing) in src/utils/quote.js returns null for any entry missing source or asOf, and the page then shows 'ask for a quote' instead of a number. tests/quote.test.mjs covers both branches.
AC3: The national benchmark is shown as a cited comparison labelled national, not Iowa.
AC4: The output lists the inputs and assumptions used and is labelled an estimate. No percentage savings appears without a stated mechanism.
AC5: 'Email me this estimate' and 'Book my assessment' submit through LEAP-001 with type='quote' and the full input payload. Booking opens Calendly prefilled with name and email.
AC6: The 0.25 constants and the employees*15 / employees*4*12 multipliers are removed from PrintCostCalculator.jsx and Tools.jsx or moved into pricing.js with sources; both pages link to /quote.
AC7: Business gate: Infomax signs off every pricing.js band before launch, recorded as confirmedBy and a date in the file.

Competitive rationale: Marco, Access Systems, Gordon Flesch and EO Johnson publish no prices on the pages checked; aggregators win cost queries with bands. https://1800officesolutions.com/copier-lease-rates/ https://www.eojohnson.com/locations/des-moines-iowa
Success metric: quote completions per week, and the share that leave contact details (target 25%); organic entrances on cost-intent queries.

stories.title: Free fleet and print-server assessment with a shareable report URL
stories.problem: Dealers lead with a no-obligation assessment that produces a written report and a review meeting, but none of the Iowa dealers checked offers it self-serve. Iowa Print Solutions has the inputs (the Tools.jsx device calculator, the print-server risk posts EliminatePrintServersIowa.jsx and PrintServerAttackSurfaceIowa.jsx, and securityAdvisories in src/config/products.js) but no assessment offer. The B2B buyer also has to sell internally: an IT director needs something to forward to a CFO or a school board. The outcome is an intake (fleet size, device makes, print servers, identity provider, current PaperCut/uniFLOW/Vasion version, pain points) that renders a vendor-neutral, source-cited report on screen and at a stable URL. The report link carries the Iowa Print Solutions name to the economic buyer.
notes: AC1: src/pages/Assessment.jsx is routed at /assessment, with a multi-step intake whose step state survives a refresh (sessionStorage inside try/catch).

AC2: Submitting creates a LEAP-001 lead (type='assessment') and returns a report id; the report is served at /assessment/report/:id by a Pages Function reading D1, with an unguessable id (128-bit random).
AC3: Report sections (print-server exposure, version and patch status from securityAdvisories, consolidation opportunity, next steps) each cite their source the way VerifiedReleaseFacts.jsx does.
AC4: The report page has a print stylesheet and a copy-link control, carries noindex, and shows no contact details.
AC5: The Navbar entry from LEAP-001 and the CTA blocks at the end of the two print-server posts link to /assessment.

AC6: The report body is built by a pure function buildReport(intake, products) in src/utils/assessment.js; tests/assessment.test.mjs asserts every section of a fixture report carries a source URL and that an unknown version yields 'cannot determine', not 'patched'.

Competitive rationale: assessments are the category's standard entry offer, but on the pages checked they are booked, not self-serve or forwardable. https://www.marconet.com/blog/why-do-a-print-assessment-for-managed-print https://www.standleys.com/managed-print-services-assessment
Success metric: assessments started vs completed, reports opened from a second device or IP (forward rate), and assessments that become a booked review meeting.

stories.title: Lead-to-deal attribution and a lead-volume dashboard for Infomax
stories.problem: Lead value is declared twice and disagrees: LEAD_VALUES in src/utils/analyticsConfig.js:47 (CONTACT_FORM 50, QUOTE_REQUEST 100 and so on) and a second LEAD_VALUES in src/components/AnalyticsProvider.jsx:9 that trackLead actually uses. Neither joins a visitor to an inquiry or an inquiry to a deal, so lead volume, the stated big move, is unmeasured. The outcome is a lead id that runs from GA4 event to D1 row to outcome. A token-protected endpoint lets Infomax sales mark each lead qualified, quoted, won or lost with a deal value, and an internal page shows leads by source and tool, stage conversion and won value. Each LEAP tool can then be judged on deals, not clicks.
notes: AC1: One LEAD_VALUES declaration remains, imported by AnalyticsProvider.jsx; grep finds a single definition.
AC2: functions/api/lead-outcome.js accepts {leadId, stage, value?} only with a valid bearer token from a Pages secret; a request without it gets 401 and writes nothing.
AC3: A lead_outcomes D1 table is append-only: stage history is kept and never overwritten.

AC4: /internal/leads (noindex, behind Cloudflare Access) shows weekly leads by type and source, stage conversion and won value. A source with no leads renders 0; a failed D1 read renders 'unavailable', never 0.
AC5: UTM parameters, gclid and the landing page are captured on first visit (sessionStorage in try/catch) and attached to every LEAP-001 lead; each GA4 lead event carries lead_id.
AC6: tests/outcomes.test.mjs posts fixture leads and outcomes against a stub D1 and asserts the dashboard aggregation, including the 0 vs unavailable distinction.
Competitive rationale: none on the competitor side is claimed; this is the instrument that tells Infomax which of the other stories produce revenue.
Success metric: share of leads with a recorded outcome (target over 70%) and won value attributed to each tool.

stories.title: Copier lease trap checker that turns renewal dates into timed leads
stories.problem: The recurring complaints about copier leases are auto-renewal clauses with short notice windows, annual payment escalators, return-shipping fees and overage click rates. None of the Iowa dealer sites checked addresses them. The outcome is a free tool at /tools/lease-checker: the visitor enters lease start, term, notice window, monthly payment, escalator and mono/color click rates, and gets the cancel-by deadline, the projected cost of missing it, and red flags against cited benchmarks. Every renewal date entered is a lead with a known buying window, and the tool positions Iowa Print Solutions on the buyer's side.
notes: AC1: src/pages/tools/LeaseChecker.jsx is routed at /tools/lease-checker and linked from /tools.
AC2: The cancel-by calculation is a pure function in src/utils/lease.js; tests/lease.test.mjs covers month-end starts, leap years and 30/60/90/180-day notice windows.
AC3: Every red-flag threshold lives in src/config/leaseBenchmarks.js with a source URL and asOf, and is displayed with that source; a threshold without a source does not render.
AC4: The cost of missing the window uses the visitor's own payment and escalator, with the formula shown.

AC5: 'Remind me before my deadline' submits through LEAP-001 with type='lease' and the computed deadline, with explicit consent copy. Until LEAP-012 sending exists the copy says Infomax will contact them, not that an automatic reminder will arrive.
AC6: A .ics file for the deadline downloads client-side with no lead required.

Competitive rationale: the clause patterns are documented by third parties; no Iowa dealer page checked publishes a checker. https://www.ecopiersolutions.com/blog/how-to-get-out-of-a-bad-copier-lease-10-step-strategic-exit-guide https://1800officesolutions.com/copier-lease-rates/
Success metric: checker completions, reminder opt-ins, and leads whose cancel-by date falls within 180 days.

stories.title: Fixed-scope service packages buyers can order from the site, starting with PaperCut v23-and-earlier upgrades
stories.problem: Everything Iowa Print Solutions offers ends in an open-ended 'free consultation', and so does every competitor. The site already documents three jobs with a defined scope and a deadline: the August 2026 PaperCut advisory in src/config/products.js states that installations on v23 or earlier get no patch and must upgrade; EliminatePrintServersIowa.jsx and PrintServerAttackSurfaceIowa.jsx make the case for retiring Windows print servers; and the emergency-patch posts describe applying a cumulative patch. The outcome is a /packages page with three fixed-scope offers (unsupported-version upgrade, emergency patch, print-server retirement), each with what is included, what is not, prerequisites, typical duration and an Infomax-confirmed price or price band, ordered through a short request flow. A buyer facing an unpatchable server can commit in one visit instead of waiting for a discovery call.
notes: AC1: src/pages/Packages.jsx is routed at /packages with one section per package, in the sitemap, using ServiceSchema.jsx.

AC2: Package definitions live in src/config/packages.js with {id, scope, excludes, prerequisites, duration, price, confirmedBy, asOf}; a package without confirmedBy renders 'price on request' instead of a number. tests/packages.test.mjs asserts that.

AC3: SecurityAdvisoryBanner.jsx and SecurityAdvisoryDetail.jsx link the upgrade package whenever the advisory's affected text names an unpatched branch, so the link appears and disappears with the config entry.
AC4: 'Request this package' submits through LEAP-001 with type='package', the package id and the visitor's product version.
AC5: Business gate: Infomax confirms scope and price for each package before it shows a number.

Competitive rationale: on the dealer pages checked, every offer is consultative and unpriced; a defined, priced package is the shortest path from an advisory search to a signed job. https://www.marconet.com/ https://www.gflesch.com/cedar-falls-ia-copiers
Success metric: package requests per month by package, and request-to-signed rate.

stories.title: Print-server retirement planner, with Universal Print fit stated honestly
stories.problem: Retiring Windows print servers is the strongest recurring theme on Iowa Print Solutions (EliminatePrintServersIowa, PrintServerAttackSurfaceIowa, UniversalPrintV2Iowa2026, the PaperCut Print Deploy facts in products.js), but every one of those pages ends in a mailto. A district or hospital IT lead needs a plan, not another article. The outcome is a planner at /tools/print-server-retirement: the visitor enters server count, queue count, client OS mix (including ARM64, which products.js says Print Deploy now handles), identity provider, M365 licence tier and whether they need secure release or cost recovery. It returns a phased plan naming which options fit (Universal Print, PaperCut Print Deploy, Vasion Print, uniFLOW) with disqualifiers, and says plainly when Universal Print alone is enough. The plan ends in the LEAP-006 retirement package.
notes: AC1: src/pages/tools/PrintServerRetirement.jsx is routed and linked from the two print-server posts, UniversalPrintV2Iowa2026.jsx, /tools and both industry pages.
AC2: Option rules live in src/config/retirementRules.js and reference feature ids in products.js; tests/retirement.test.mjs fails if a rule points at a feature id that does not exist.
AC3: Universal Print quota and preview-stage features are added to products.js with Microsoft Learn sources and an asOf date before the planner uses them.
AC4: A 'Universal Print covers this' result renders with no upsell block in that branch (asserted in the test on the plan object).
AC5: 'Send me this plan' and 'Price the retirement' submit through LEAP-001 with type='retirement_plan' and the answers.

Competitive rationale: Microsoft and Vasion each market only their own product, and the Iowa dealer pages checked do not address print-server retirement as a self-serve plan. https://learn.microsoft.com/universal-print/whats-new https://vasion.com/launches/spring-launch-2026/
Success metric: plans completed, plan-to-lead rate, and retirement package requests sourced from the planner.

stories.title: Patch-status checker: am I exposed?
stories.problem: When a PaperCut CVE lands, admins search for whether their version is affected. Iowa Print Solutions holds that data in securityAdvisories in src/config/products.js, but the affected versions are prose (the August 2026 entry's affected field is one sentence naming v24, v25 and v26 branches), so visitors have to read and interpret it. The outcome is a tool at /tools/patch-check: pick a product, enter a version, see which tracked advisories apply, the fixed patch and the vendor source, then request patch help or the LEAP-006 upgrade package. It is the fastest route from an emergency search to a conversation.
notes: AC1: src/pages/tools/PatchCheck.jsx is routed at /tools/patch-check and linked from SecurityAdvisoryBanner.jsx and every advisory post.

AC2: Each securityAdvisories entry gains machine-readable affectedRanges and fixedIn fields beside the existing prose; tests/advisories.test.mjs fails if any entry lacks them, so the checker cannot silently skip one.

AC3: Version comparison is a pure function in src/utils/version.js; tests cover PaperCut dotted versions, branch-only input ('v23') and unknown formats. An unparseable version returns 'cannot determine', never 'not affected'.
AC4: A clean result reads 'not affected by advisories we track as of <FACTS_VERIFIED>', never 'secure'.
AC5: 'Get patch help' submits through LEAP-001 with type='patch_help', product and version.
Competitive rationale: the advisory corpus with patch branches is already on the site and no Iowa dealer page checked publishes one; the checker turns it into capture.
Success metric: checks run per advisory event, share returning an exposed result, and patch_help leads.

stories.title: Managed print and MFP hardware line, with service levels Infomax actually commits to
stories.problem: Infomax is an MFP dealer, but Iowa Print Solutions sells only software: imageRUNNER appears nowhere in src/pages, there is no copier leasing or managed print offer page, and managed print appears as one blog post (ManagedPrintServicesIowa.jsx). Competitors sell device-plus-service bundles. Meanwhile Contact.jsx states service commitments with no stated basis: '24/7 emergency support', '2-4 hours' response and 'on-site service ... within 24-48 hours' (lines 100, 116, 120, 147, 223, 488), while siteConfig.hours says 08:00-17:00 weekdays, closed weekends. The outcome is an offer line (/managed-print-services, /copier-leasing) built on Infomax-confirmed hardware lines and service levels, so a software lead can expand into a fleet contract and every service promise on the site is one Infomax will stand behind.
notes: AC1: src/pages/services/ManagedPrintServices.jsx and src/pages/services/CopierLeasing.jsx are routed, in the sitemap, and use ServiceSchema.jsx.
AC2: Brand and model claims come from src/config/hardware.js listing only lines Infomax confirms it sells, each with a vendor source URL; an entry without confirmedBy does not render.

AC3: Service levels live in src/config/serviceLevels.js with confirmedBy and asOf; the Contact.jsx FAQ and the new pages render from it, and any promise Infomax does not confirm is removed. A test asserts no '24/7' or 'hour' response promise remains in Contact.jsx outside serviceLevels-driven text.
AC4: Lease terms reuse LEAP-005's benchmark config and link to the lease checker.
AC5: Results in the Tools.jsx device calculator, /quote and the assessment report show a fleet-consolidation next step linking to these pages; both pages end in IntakeCTA with type='mps'.
AC6: Services.jsx and the Navbar Services menu list the new line.

Competitive rationale: Access Systems holds Iowa State procurement copier contracts and Gordon Flesch leads with copier hardware on its Iowa pages; device-plus-service is how incumbents win. https://www.procurement.iastate.edu/node/12?id=70 https://www.gflesch.com/cedar-falls-ia-copiers
Success metric: MPS and hardware leads per month, and the share of software leads that add a fleet scope.

stories.title: Paid search to the self-serve tools, with offline conversions fed back to Google Ads
stories.problem: Organic search is slow and RENDER-1 (pre-rendering) is still todo, so the self-serve tools will take months to rank. Cost and lease queries are exactly the ones aggregators buy. Iowa Print Solutions runs no paid acquisition, and even if it did, Google Ads would optimise for form fills because nothing reports which leads became deals. The outcome is a small, measured paid search program: Iowa-geo campaigns pointed at /quote, /tools/lease-checker, /tools/patch-check and /assessment, gclid stored on each lead, and won deals from LEAP-004 uploaded as offline conversions so bidding learns from revenue rather than clicks.
notes: AC1: gclid and gbraid/wbraid are captured on landing (LEAP-004 AC5) and stored on the lead row; tests assert they survive to D1.

AC2: functions/api/ads-export.js (bearer-token protected, same pattern as lead-outcome) returns won and qualified outcomes in Google Ads offline conversion CSV format; a lead without a click id is excluded and counted in a separate field rather than dropped silently.
AC3: Landing variants for paid traffic carry noindex and reuse the tool pages; no duplicate indexable content is created.
AC4: docs/paid-search.md records campaign structure, negative keywords, the Iowa geo target, and the monthly budget Infomax approves. Business gate: no campaign launches without that budget recorded.
AC5: /internal/leads splits leads and won value by paid vs organic.

Competitive rationale: aggregators buy cost-intent queries and resell leads; a local dealer bidding on its own tools with revenue feedback competes on cost per deal, not cost per click. https://1800officesolutions.com/copier-lease-rates/
Success metric: cost per qualified lead and cost per won deal by campaign, against a ceiling Infomax sets.

stories.title: Security and release alert list for Iowa print admins
stories.problem: securityAdvisories in src/config/products.js, rendered by SecurityAdvisoryDetail.jsx and SecurityAdvisoryBanner.jsx, plus posts like PaperCutEmergencyPatchIowa.jsx, PaperCutPatchIowaSchools.jsx and PaperCutPatchIowaHealthcare.jsx, make Iowa Print Solutions a fast, cited, Iowa-specific advisory source. It is the one content type with urgency and a reason to come back, and it captures nobody: no signup, no feed. The outcome is a consented subscription ('PaperCut, uniFLOW and Vasion security and release notices for Iowa admins') plus a public feed, so each new advisory reaches the admins who run those fleets, including existing Infomax customers who need patches and renewals.
notes: AC1: A subscribe component (product checkboxes, email, explicit consent text) appears on SecurityAdvisoryBanner.jsx surfaces and on every advisory post; it submits through LEAP-001 with type='advisory_subscribe'.
AC2: Double opt-in: the subscription is inactive until a confirmation link is clicked; the record stores consent basis, source page and timestamp.

AC3: scripts/generate-advisory-feed.mjs runs in prebuild beside generate-sitemap.mjs and writes public/advisories.xml and public/advisories.json from securityAdvisories; tests assert every advisory appears in both.
AC4: Every email carries a one-click unsubscribe that works without login and is honoured before the next send.
AC5: The sending identity is a separate verified subdomain, not DPearson@InfomaxOffice.com, documented in docs/; until it is configured the UI says 'feed only' and promises no email.
AC6: public/llms.txt links the feed.

Competitive rationale: vendors announce releases globally and the Iowa dealer pages checked run generic blogs; none offers a product-specific advisory list. https://www.papercut.com/blog/releases/new-in-papercut-hive-and-pocket-march-2026/
Success metric: confirmed subscribers by product, and advisory emails that produce a patch_help or package lead.

stories.title: Consented lifecycle email for quotes, assessments, lease deadlines and advisories
stories.problem: The self-serve tools create leads with different buying windows: a lease deadline nine months out, a quote this week, an advisory subscriber who is not buying. Without timed follow-up those leads cool, and one personal inbox cannot track timing. The outcome is a scheduled sender (a Cloudflare Cron Trigger on a Worker sharing the LEAP-001 D1 database) that sends only what the visitor consented to: the quote or report copy, lease reminders at 90/60/30 days before cancel-by, and advisory notices. Every send is recorded against the lead. The lease reminder lands when the buyer can actually switch.
notes: AC1: The cron job reads due sends from a D1 sends table and records each attempt with status; a failed send stays retryable and is never marked sent.
AC2: Each send type requires a matching consent record from LEAP-001; a lead without consent for that type is skipped and the skip is logged with its reason.
AC3: Lease reminder dates are computed by a pure function reusing src/utils/lease.js from LEAP-005; tests cover 90/60/30-day offsets across month ends.
AC4: One-click unsubscribe per type, honoured before the next cron run (asserted in a test that unsubscribes then runs the scheduler against a stub).
AC5: The sender identity is the LEAP-011 subdomain, documented in docs/.
AC6: Email copy follows the repo's editorial standard: no unsourced numbers.
Competitive rationale: auto-renewal clauses depend on the buyer missing the window; a reminder is the counter. https://www.aopinc.com/blog/questions-before-signing-copier-lease
Success metric: reminder-to-meeting rate, unsubscribe rate under 2% per send, and won deals sourced from reminders.

stories.title: Make the resource library real: six gated guides generated from the verified corpus
stories.problem: /resource-library advertises six downloads in ResourceLibrary.jsx (Buyer's Guide at line 26, HIPAA checklist at 40, K-12 toolkit at 54, cost reduction guide at 68, security best practices at 82, and at 96-97 an 'Advanced Excel spreadsheet' ROI calculator), and no backing file exists in public/. The visitors who ask for a buyer's guide are among the highest-intent on the site, and today they get an alert() and nothing. The outcome is real assets, generated where possible from products.js so they stay current, delivered after a LEAP-001 capture. Any title that cannot be produced is removed rather than promised.
notes: AC1: Each resource listed in ResourceLibrary.jsx maps to a real file or generated route; tests/resources.test.mjs fails if a listed resource has no backing asset.
AC2: The Buyer's Guide and HIPAA checklist are generated at build time by scripts/build-resources.mjs from products.js and carry FACTS_VERIFIED.
AC3: The 'Advanced Excel spreadsheet' is either a real .xlsx whose formulas use the LEAP-002 pricing.js bands, or the entry is removed.
AC4: A type='resource' lead returns a signed, expiring download link, shown on screen and emailed once LEAP-011's sender exists.
AC5: The download path is excluded from the sitemap and disallowed in public/robots.txt.
AC6: Each asset ends with the assessment CTA.

Competitive rationale: Marco gates ebooks and case studies behind forms; Iowa Print Solutions currently gates nothing real. https://www.marconet.com/ebooks/managed-print-services-case-study-collection/des-moines-public-schools
Success metric: resource downloads per week, and resource leads that later book an assessment.

stories.title: Product-fit wizard: PaperCut, uniFLOW, Vasion or Universal Print
stories.problem: PrintManagementComparison.jsx assigns a fixed 'Recommended:' product to three static use cases (lines 56-70), and the comparison content is spread across PaperCutVsUniflowComparison, PrintManagementSoftwareComparison and three '-vs-' blog posts. Backlog item 6 in docs/SEO-GEO-STRATEGY.md plans the comparison as flagship content; nothing answers the visitor's own situation. The outcome is a deterministic questionnaire at /which-print-management (fleet makes, M365 licensing, cloud vs on-prem, badge release, cost recovery, HIPAA/FERPA, size) that answers from products.js with stated disqualifiers and ends in the assessment. It is the interactive layer over item 6, not a second article.
notes: AC1: src/pages/tools/ProductFit.jsx is routed at /which-print-management and linked from /print-management-comparison, /tools and the three comparison posts.
AC2: Rules live in src/config/productFit.js; each references a feature id in products.js, and tests/productfit.test.mjs fails on a rule pointing at a missing feature.
AC3: Every recommendation lists why and why not, each with a source link; Universal Print is an option, using the quota facts LEAP-007 adds to products.js.
AC4: A tie returns 'two fit, here is the deciding question' rather than a forced pick (covered in the test).
AC5: The static 'Recommended:' cards in PrintManagementComparison.jsx link into the wizard with their use case preselected.
AC6: The result offers 'send me this' and 'book an assessment' through LEAP-001 with type='product_fit' and the answers.

Competitive rationale: Gordon Flesch's PaperCut vs uniFLOW post is a two-way 2022 article; Vasion and Microsoft market only themselves. https://gflesch.com/blog/comparing-papercut-vs.-uniflow-print-management-software
Success metric: wizard completions, result-to-lead rate, and rankings for 'PaperCut vs uniFLOW' class queries.

stories.title: Iowa public-procurement hub: buying through contract vehicles a buyer already has
stories.problem: Iowa schools and agencies buy through AEA Purchasing, the Iowa DAS cooperative purchasing program and university procurement contracts; Access Systems appears on Iowa State's procurement contract list. 'How an Iowa district buys print management through a contract it already has' is high-intent, and no competitor page checked explains it. The K-12 posts (PaperCutMF26K12Iowa, SchoolDistrictIowa, PaperCutPatchIowaSchools) end in a mailto. The outcome is /iowa-procurement explaining each vehicle, what it covers and how Infomax fits, gated on which vehicles Infomax actually holds, ending in a procurement-ready quote request.
notes: AC1: src/pages/IowaProcurement.jsx is routed and linked from IowaEducationPrintSolutions.jsx and the three K-12 posts.

AC2: Vehicles live in src/config/procurement.js with {name, scope, source, infomaxHolds: true|false|null, confirmedAsOf}; null renders 'contact us to confirm', never a claim. A test asserts no vehicle renders as held without confirmedAsOf.
AC3: Each vehicle links its official source page.
AC4: A procurement quote request captures organization, vehicle and timeline through LEAP-001 with type='procurement'.
AC5: FAQ schema is added through FAQSchema.jsx.
AC6: Business gate: Infomax confirms every infomaxHolds value before launch.

Competitive rationale: public-sector contracts are an incumbent's lock-in; explaining the vehicles is the way in. https://www.ghaea.org/administrators/aea-purchasing/ https://das.iowa.gov/state-employees/procurement/cooperative-purchasing-program https://www.procurement.iastate.edu/node/12?id=70
Success metric: procurement leads from public-sector email domains, and entrances on contract-vehicle queries.

stories.title: Segment x product x Iowa-fact pages for the verticals llms.txt claims
stories.problem: public/llms.txt (lines 10-11) claims healthcare, K-12 and higher education, manufacturing, financial services, government and legal, but src/pages/industries holds only IowaEducationPrintSolutions.jsx and IowaHealthcarePrintSolutions.jsx. The strategy doc's page-architecture rules forbid find-and-replace pages, so the defensible axis is segment x product x one substantive Iowa fact a national reseller cannot write (for example uniFLOW for Board of Regents institutions, secure print for Iowa law firms). This is separate from backlog item 8 (Central Iowa city pages). The outcome is a data-driven set rendered by EnhancedIndustryTemplate.jsx that captures long-tail intent and makes llms.txt true.
notes: AC1: src/data/segments.js defines each page as {segment, product, iowaFact, factSource, compliance, ctaType}, and EnhancedIndustryTemplate.jsx renders from it.
AC2: tests/segments.test.mjs fails if an entry lacks iowaFact or factSource.
AC3: At least four new pages ship (manufacturing, financial services, government, legal); any segment without a sourced Iowa fact is dropped from llms.txt instead of shipped thin.
AC4: Each page links to the product-fit wizard (LEAP-014) and the assessment (LEAP-003).
AC5: The industry list in llms.txt matches the routed industry pages exactly (a test compares them).
AC6: The test rejects any two segment pages sharing more than 40% of body text by shingle overlap.
Competitive rationale: the Iowa dealer pages checked carry generic industry copy without a product-plus-Iowa-fact angle. https://www.gflesch.com/cedar-falls-ia-copiers
Success metric: organic entrances and leads per segment page within 90 days.

stories.title: Referral program for Iowa MSPs and IT consultants who do not sell print
stories.problem: Most Iowa managed IT providers and independent consultants support the networks and identity systems print management depends on, but do not sell PaperCut, uniFLOW or MFP fleets, and they field the print-server and patch questions anyway. Iowa Print Solutions has no channel for them, so their referrals go to whichever dealer they happen to know. The outcome is a /partners page with a referral agreement, per-partner referral links that tag every LEAP-001 lead with a partner code, a partner-facing status view for their referrals, and co-branded copies of the assessment report and patch checker the partner can send their clients. A channel that brings pre-qualified leads is one the big dealers do not court, because those MSPs often compete with them on managed IT.
notes: AC1: src/pages/Partners.jsx is routed at /partners with the program terms rendered from src/config/partners.js; terms without confirmedBy do not render, and the page then offers only 'talk to us about referring'.
AC2: A ?ref=<code> parameter is persisted for the session and stored on the lead; tests assert it reaches the D1 row and that an unknown code is stored as unknown rather than dropped.
AC3: /partners/status (token link per partner, noindex) lists that partner's referrals with stage from LEAP-004 and no other partner's data; a test asserts isolation.
AC4: The assessment report (LEAP-003) and patch checker (LEAP-008) accept the ref code and show 'shared by <partner>' on the shared view.
AC5: Business gate: Infomax approves the referral fee or credit and the agreement text before launch.
Competitive rationale: Marco sells managed IT itself and so competes with the MSPs that would refer; that conflict is the opening for a print-only partner. https://www.marconet.com/
Success metric: active referring partners, referred leads per month, and referred won value.

stories.title: Fleet usage analyzer: drop in a PaperCut or uniFLOW export, get a waste report in the browser
stories.problem: Usage analytics (anomaly reporting, predictive supplies and service) is where the category is heading per Quocirca's 2026 vendor landscape, and none of the Iowa dealer sites checked offers it self-serve. Existing PaperCut and uniFLOW customers already hold the data in their usage exports. The outcome is a client-side analyzer: the visitor drops in a usage CSV and the browser computes color share, simplex share, top printers by cost, idle devices, after-hours volume and outliers. The data never leaves the device, and the report ends in a consolidation or managed print conversation grounded in the customer's own numbers.
notes: AC1: src/pages/tools/UsageAnalyzer.jsx is routed at /tools/usage-analyzer; parsing runs in a Web Worker and no request carries file contents.

AC2: Parsers in src/utils/usageParsers.js handle the documented PaperCut print log and uniFLOW export column sets, with fixture CSVs in tests/fixtures; tests/usage.test.mjs asserts the metrics on each fixture, and an unrecognised file reports which columns were expected.
AC3: Every metric shows its formula; nothing is projected to annual savings without the visitor's own cost-per-page input.
AC4: Outliers use a stated rule (over 3x the per-device median), named on screen.
AC5: 'Email me the full report' sends only the computed summary, never raw rows, through LEAP-001 with type='usage_report'; a test asserts the payload holds no row-level fields.
AC6: A privacy note states the file stays in the browser, and PrivacyPolicy.jsx is updated to match.
Competitive rationale: https://quocirca.com/content/quocirca-ai-vendor-landscape-2026/
Success metric: files analysed, summary-report lead rate, and MPS leads sourced from the analyzer.

stories.title: Iowa Print Cost Index: a quarterly benchmark built from the site's own anonymised tool data
stories.problem: Every cost figure on Iowa Print Solutions today is a national benchmark or an unsourced constant, and the strategy doc says AI answer engines reward specific, attributed claims. Once LEAP-002, LEAP-003 and LEAP-005 are live, the site will hold something no Iowa dealer publishes: real Iowa monthly volumes, color shares, lease payments and click rates entered by Iowa organizations. The outcome is a quarterly /iowa-print-cost-index page that publishes aggregate medians and ranges by segment and size band, with sample size and method stated, suppressing any cell below a minimum count. It becomes the citable local number that journalists, AI answers and other sites link to, and every chart ends in 'compare yours' (the quote builder).
notes: AC1: scripts/build-cost-index.mjs (run manually or by cron, never in the public build) reads D1, drops contact fields, and writes src/data/costIndex.json with n per cell; any cell with n below 20 is written as suppressed, not as a number.
AC2: tests/costindex.test.mjs asserts suppression below the threshold, that no contact field or lead id appears in the output, and that a cell with n=0 is absent rather than 0.
AC3: src/pages/IowaPrintCostIndex.jsx renders the index with method, sample size, period and asOf, using ArticleSchema.jsx with dateModified per edition.
AC4: The first edition is not published until at least one cell clears the threshold; until then the route does not exist.
AC5: Each LEAP-001 consent text states that anonymised, aggregated inputs may be published.
AC6: public/llms.txt lists the index.
Competitive rationale: competitors cite national figures or none; an original local dataset is the asset that earns links and AI citations rather than chasing them.
Success metric: referring domains and AI-answer citations to the index page, and quote starts from its 'compare yours' link.

stories.title: Grounded print-management answer assistant
stories.problem: Buyers increasingly ask an assistant instead of reading 45 blog posts and 18 resource guides. Iowa Print Solutions' advantage is that its product facts are dated and sourced in src/config/products.js; a general assistant cannot tell which PaperCut feature is new in 26.0 and which is long-standing, and the site can. The outcome is an 'Ask about PaperCut, uniFLOW or Vasion' assistant: a Pages Function calls a model with retrieval over products.js and the site's posts, cites the pages it used, refuses pricing beyond LEAP-002's confirmed bands and anything outside the corpus, and hands off to the intake. It ranks last because it depends on the corpus, the pricing gate and the pipeline being in place, and it carries a running cost.
notes: AC1: functions/api/ask.js accepts a question, retrieves passages from a build-time index (scripts/build-ask-index.mjs over products.js, src/pages/blog and src/pages/resources) and returns {answer, citations[]}.
AC2: An answer with zero citations is replaced by 'I don't have a verified answer; here is how to ask Infomax'.

AC3: The system prompt forbids price figures outside pricing.js and certification claims not in src/config/site.js; tests/ask.test.mjs runs adversarial prompts against a stubbed model response path and asserts the citation and price guards fire.
AC4: Per-IP rate limiting and Turnstile protect the endpoint; the model key is a Pages secret.
AC5: 'Talk to a person' creates a LEAP-001 lead carrying the transcript, only with consent.
AC6: Cost per answer is logged, with a weekly total on /internal/leads.

Competitive rationale: vendors' AI messaging is ahead of dealers'; no Iowa dealer page checked answers questions from a verified corpus. https://quocirca.com/content/quocirca-ai-vendor-landscape-2026/ https://vasion.com/whats-new/
Success metric: questions answered with citations, share escalated to a lead, and refusal rate on out-of-corpus questions.
